title: Brewster kaleidoscope
blurb: One live interactive HTML card reflected across 4-fold, 6-fold, 8-fold, 12-fold and triangular kaleidoscope mirror chambers on a single WebGL 2 canvas. Tests whether updateElementGeometry() accepts negative-determinant mirror transforms so buttons, sliders and text inputs work in reflected wedges.
question: Can one live interactive HTML card be reflected across 6-fold, 8-fold, 12-fold, and triangular kaleidoscope mirror chambers, and does Chromium's updateElementGeometry() accept negative-determinant (mirror-reflected) DOMMatrix transforms so buttons and inputs work identically in reflected wedges?
result: Not verified in a live browser yet. One ElementGL WebGL 2 context uploads the stained-glass HTML card with texElementSubImage2D(), folds screen coordinates through dihedral (D4, D6, D8, D12) and equilateral-triangle (p3m1) mirror groups with textureGrad() mipmap filtering, and reprojects rigid reflection DOMMatrix transforms (det +1 and det -1) onto updateElementGeometry() under the pointer.
